title: GPU gym
description: Write GPU kernels in CUDA, Triton or PyTorch: indexing warm-ups, coalescing and shared memory, reductions and scans, the kernels around a transformer layer, tiled matmul, flash attention, MoE, sparse rows, sorting, and FP16 Tensor Core and int8 kernels. Checked against PyTorch and benchmarked against your GPU's bandwidth or FLOP/s.

tracks.name: Warm-up: indexing and launch config
tracks.summary: One thread per element: global indices, bounds checks, grid sizes and wide loads.

tracks.name: Memory patterns
tracks.summary: Coalesced reads and writes, shared-memory tiles, and reusing what neighbouring threads load.

tracks.name: Cooperation in a block
tracks.summary: Threads working together through shared memory, warp shuffles, atomics and scans.

tracks.name: Row-wise model kernels
tracks.summary: One block per row: a reduction, then an elementwise pass, as in softmax and layer norm.

tracks.name: LLM building blocks
tracks.summary: The memory-bound kernels around a transformer layer: embeddings, fused activations, RMSNorm, rotary embeddings and the loss.

tracks.name: Compute-bound
tracks.summary: Tiling for data reuse, from a plain matmul to flash attention and the grouped matmul of a mixture-of-experts layer.

tracks.name: Data-dependent work
tracks.summary: Irregular and data-dependent kernels: sparse rows of very different lengths, selection and sorting.

tracks.name: Low precision
tracks.summary: Tensor Core matmul with FP16 inputs and an FP32 accumulator, and a matvec over int8 weights with per-row scales.
